_doc.about: Message building every client must match: web (shared/src/compose, TypeScript) and Android :core (Kotlin). Line breaks inside expected strings are exact; built messages use CRLF.
_doc.markdown:
markdownToHtml(markdown), compared after normalizeHtml, and markdownToText(markdown). The text styles are latr's (markdown-span-fixtures.json and inline-style-fixtures.json): *bold* becomes , _italic_ , both without their markers; a bare URL becomes (a www. one to http://); ![alt](cid:id) becomes ; everything else as rich-fixtures.json reads it (markdownToRich, then richToHtml): inline code, ~~strike~~, [links](url), # headings, - and 1. lists, > quotes and ``` code blocks; text is escaped (& < > "), and the line breaks between plain lines are
. normalizeHtml: replace /\s*\/>/ with '>', ''' with "'", />\s+<', then trim. Plain text is the source as typed: CRLF/CR to LF, trailing spaces and tabs removed from each line, leading and trailing blank lines removed; the HTML is rendered from that trimmed text.
_doc.body:
bodyParts(body, signature): html (normalized) is
BODY
then
SIGNATURE
; text is BODY, a blank line, '-- ' (dash dash space) and the signature. A null or blank signature adds nothing; an empty body leaves just '-- ' and the signature. With `quote` (a reply): html gains '
' + '
' + escaped attribution + '
' + (quotableHtml(html), or when html is null '
' + escaped text lines joined by '
' + '
') + '
'; text gains a blank line (unless empty so far) and quoteText(quote). quote.dateLocal is a local time.
_doc.replySubject: Kept when it starts (after trimming) with Re: in any case, or Re[n]:; else 'Re: ' + trimmed subject; empty gives 'Re:'.
_doc.forwardSubject: Kept when it starts with Fwd: or Fw: (any case); else 'Fwd: ' + trimmed; empty gives 'Fwd:'.
_doc.replyHeaders: In-Reply-To = the source's Message-ID. References = message ids (<...>) of the source's References, or when it has none its In-Reply-To if that holds exactly one id, then the source's own id last; each id once, with no limit on how many. Null when the source's Message-ID holds no <id> (an id is <, then one or more characters that are not <, >, whitespace or a control character, then >): nothing of a raw value is copied.
_doc.recipients: replyRecipients(original, own, replyAll): see shared/src/compose/reply.ts. Addresses compare trimmed and lower-cased; own addresses never appear; first occurrence wins.
_doc.replyFrom: replyFromAddress(original, own, fallback): the first own address found in To then Cc, as spelled in `own`; else fallback.
_doc.mailbox: formatMailbox: no name -> address; printable ASCII words -> 'Name <addr>'; ASCII with specials ()<>[]:;@\,." or a run of spaces -> quoted string with \ and " backslash-escaped; non-ASCII or containing '=?' -> RFC 2047 B words (UTF-8, at most 45 bytes each, never splitting a character) joined by spaces. Names and the address are trimmed first.
_doc.headerText: encodeHeaderText: printable ASCII without '=?' is unchanged; anything else becomes B encoded words as for names.
_doc.fold: foldHeader(name, value): 'Name: value' split at single spaces into lines of at most 78 characters where possible, continuation lines starting with one space, joined by CRLF; a word is never split.
_doc.qp: quotedPrintable(text) over UTF-8, CRLF line breaks; bytes 33-60 and 62-126 literal; space and tab literal unless last on the line; others =XX upper-case; soft break '=' when the line would pass 75 characters; escapes never split.
_doc.base64Lines: Standard base64 with padding of the UTF-8 bytes of `utf8`, 76 characters per line, CRLF between lines, no trailing break.
_doc.mime: buildMime(input): file `data` fields here are standard base64 of the bytes. Expected is the exact message text. Boundaries are =_<boundary>_0 for the outermost multipart, counting inward. input.quote, when present, carries dateLocal (a local time) in place of date.
_doc.attribution: quoteAttribution(from, date) in the device's zone (fixtures: America/New_York), 24-hour: 'On <Ddd>, <Mmm> <d>, <yyyy> at <HH:mm>, <Name> <<email>> wrote:'; English abbreviations; day of month without padding; a blank (after trimming) name gives '<<email>>' alone. dateLocal is a local time.
_doc.quoteText: quoteText(quote): attribution, a blank line, then the original text (CRLF/CR to LF, trailing spaces/tabs trimmed per line, leading/trailing blank lines dropped) with each line as '> ' + line and a blank line as '>'. With no text left, just the attribution.
_doc.quotableHtml: quotableHtml(html): the inside of <body> if present (to </body> or the end), then remove <!doctype>, comments, <head>...</head>, <script>...</script> and any <html>/<body> tags left; trim.
_doc.splitText: splitQuotedText(text) -> { body, quote }: see shared/src/compose/quote.ts. A line '-----Original Message-----' (2+ dashes each side, any case) starts a quote to the end. Otherwise the trailing run of '>' lines (blank lines inside allowed, only blank lines after) is a quote when the nearest non-blank line above ends with ':' (that line, or the line before too when it starts with 'On ' and this one doesn't, is the attribution). body is the text above, trailing whitespace removed; quote runs from the attribution, trailing whitespace removed. No quote (body = input, quote = null) without an attribution or when body would be blank. Input line breaks are normalized to LF first.
_doc.splitHtml: splitQuotedHtml(html) -> { body, quote }: see shared/src/compose/quote.ts. Markers, matched case-insensitively at an opening tag: div/blockquote with class gmail_quote or gmail_quote_container; blockquote type=cite; div class moz-cite-prefix or yahoo_quoted; div id divRplyFwdMsg or appendonsend (Outlook: the quote runs to the end whatever follows). An element ends at its matching close tag, counting nested tags of the same name (the end of input if unclosed). The quote starts at the first marker after whose element all visible text (tags,
_doc.quotedContentIds: quotedContentIds(html): the Content-IDs the quoted original's HTML refers to as cid: URLs, in order of first use, each once, looking only at quotableHtml(html). A cid: URL ends at a quote, whitespace, ')', '>' or ';', and is percent-decoded (kept as is when decoding fails). null html gives []. The reply attaches those inline parts of the original again, with the same Content-ID.
_doc.invalidMailbox: formatMailbox(mailbox) must throw (InvalidAddressError; Android: its own typed error) when the trimmed address isn't exactly one '@' with text on each side, or holds whitespace (JavaScript \s: Unicode spaces too, e.g. U+00A0), a control character, ',', ';', '<' or '>'. buildMime throws the same error for any such From/To/Cc/Bcc.
_doc.answerHeaders: answerHeaders(source, forward): subject is replySubject(source.subject), or forwardSubject with forward; In-Reply-To and References are replyHeaders(source)'s, or null and [] when source.messageId holds no <id> (blank, or a raw value such as one smuggling a line break). mime is the header lines buildMime writes for them, from Subject up to MIME-Version, CRLF-joined, with from {name:'', email:'test@hafa.cc'}, to [{name:'', email:'bob@example.com'}], body 'Hi', no signature, no extra headers, boundary 'b0'.
_doc.offersReplyAll: offersReplyAll(original, own): true when replyRecipients(original, own, replyAll = true) has more than one address in to and cc together. The open thread offers Reply all for its last message only then.
_doc.invalidHeader: buildMime(input) must throw (InvalidHeaderError; Android: its own typed error) when any header value it writes holds a control character other than tab (Unicode Cc: U+0000-U+001F except U+0009, U+007F-U+009F), CR and LF included: In-Reply-To, References, extraHeaders, a file's mimeType or Content-ID, a calendar method. Inputs are as in mime.
